code.originalText: Twenty-three-week review: remission, smoking, blood pressure and lipids

text.paragraph: Twenty-three-week review: remission, smoking, blood pressure and lipids. [S]

Dr. King returns six weeks after a bronchitis, which settled in about two weeks without an antibiotic; he did not smoke through it. He has been smoke-free since the June lapse and is five weeks into the second course of varenicline. His mood has been good for over a month, he sleeps about seven hours, and therapy is now monthly. He has kept most of his work plan, though the autumn schedule is heavier. Home readings averaged 128/82. He has lost about a kilogram. He has no thoughts of harming himself. [S]

tr.td: Blood pressure 128/82, pulse 70; weight 82.8 kg, BMI 28.7

Exhaustion, broken sleep and low mood for about two months, under sustained threats and a punishing schedule, after an admission for exhaustion and a respiratory infection six months ago; cause not established at intake: a depressive disorder, an adjustment disorder, PTSD, an insomnia disorder, thyroid disease and anemia to be assessed; psychiatry consultation requested
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented admission for exhaustion and the threats against him; superseded by the diagnoses at the second visit.
Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate (DSM-5-TR), arising under chronic threat, surveillance and overwork; no suicidal ideation; PTSD not present on screening and interview

S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the psychiatry consultation, linked to his documented exhaustion and threats and to biographers' accounts of depression (R); not a claim that he was so diagnosed.

S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the psychiatry consultation.
